## Setup

```{python}
# Import required libraries
import polars as pl
import polars.selectors as cs
import numpy as np
from plotnine import *

# Set display options
pl.Config.set_tbl_rows(10)
```

## Load Data

```{python}
# Load the fully imputed training data (zero missing values)
# Note: infer_schema_length=None scans entire file to correctly infer data types
df_train = pl.read_csv(
    "application_train_fully_imputed.csv",
    infer_schema_length=None
)

# Display dataset shape and first few rows
print(f"Training data shape: {df_train.shape}")
print(f"Total missing values: {df_train.null_count().sum_horizontal()[0]}")
print("\n✅ Successfully loaded fully imputed data!")
print("\nFirst few rows:")
df_train.head()
```

```{python}
# Check the target variable distribution
target_dist = (
    df_train
    .group_by("TARGET")
    .agg(pl.len().alias("count"))
    .with_columns(
        percentage=(pl.col("count") / df_train.height * 100).round(2)
    )
    .sort("TARGET")
)

print("Target variable distribution:")
target_dist
```

```{python}
# Visualize class imbalance
(
    ggplot(df_train.to_pandas(), aes(x="factor(TARGET)", fill="factor(TARGET)"))

    + labs(
        title="Target Variable Distribution",
        x="Target (0=Repaid, 1=Default)",
```

## Baseline Performance: Majority Class Classifier

Before building complex models, let's establish a baseline by predicting the majority class (0 = repaid) for all observations.

```{python}
from sklearn.metrics import accuracy_score, roc_auc_score, confusion_matrix, classification_report

# Create baseline predictions (always predict majority class: 0)
y_true = df_train.get_column("TARGET").to_numpy()
y_pred_baseline = np.zeros(len(y_true))  # Always predict 0 (repaid)

# For AUC, we need probabilities - majority class gets probability 1.0
y_prob_baseline = np.zeros(len(y_true))  # Probability of class 1 (default) = 0

# Calculate baseline metrics
baseline_accuracy = accuracy_score(y_true, y_pred_baseline)
baseline_auc = roc_auc_score(y_true, y_prob_baseline)

print("=" * 70)
print("BASELINE PERFORMANCE: MAJORITY CLASS CLASSIFIER")
print("=" * 70)
print(f"\nStrategy: Always predict class 0 (Repaid)")
print(f"\nAccuracy: {baseline_accuracy:.4f} ({baseline_accuracy*100:.2f}%)")
print(f"AUC-ROC:  {baseline_auc:.4f}")
print("\nConfusion Matrix:")
print(confusion_matrix(y_true, y_pred_baseline))
print("\nClassification Report:")
print(classification_report(y_true, y_pred_baseline, target_names=["Repaid", "Default"]))
print("=" * 70)
print("\n📌 Key Insight: Any model must beat {:.2f}% accuracy to be useful!".format(baseline_accuracy*100))
print("📌 AUC of 0.50 means random guessing - we need significantly higher!")
```

## Data Preparation for Modeling

### Separate Features and Target

```{python}
# Separate features (X) and target (y)
# Exclude SK_ID_CURR (ID column) and TARGET (our label)
feature_cols = [col for col in df_train.columns if col not in ["SK_ID_CURR", "TARGET"]]

X = df_train.select(feature_cols)
y = df_train.get_column("TARGET").to_numpy()

print(f"Features shape: {X.shape}")
print(f"Target shape: {y.shape}")
print(f"\nNumber of features: {len(feature_cols)}")
```

### Encode Categorical Variables

```{python}
# Identify categorical columns (string type)
cat_cols = [col for col in X.columns if X[col].dtype == pl.Utf8]
num_cols = [col for col in X.columns if col not in cat_cols]

print(f"Categorical columns: {len(cat_cols)}")
print(f"Numeric columns: {len(num_cols)}")
print(f"\nCategorical columns: {cat_cols}")
```

```{python}
# One-hot encode categorical variables
# Convert to pandas for sklearn compatibility
X_pd = X.to_pandas()

# One-hot encode
X_encoded = pd.get_dummies(X_pd, columns=cat_cols, drop_first=True)

print(f"\nOriginal features: {X_pd.shape[1]}")
print(f"After one-hot encoding: {X_encoded.shape[1]}")
print(f"New dummy features created: {X_encoded.shape[1] - X_pd.shape[1]}")
```

### Train/Validation Split

```{python}
from sklearn.model_selection import train_test_split

# Split data: 80% train, 20% validation
X_train, X_val, y_train, y_val = train_test_split(
    X_encoded, 
    y, 
    test_size=0.2, 
    random_state=42,
    stratify=y  # Maintain class distribution
)

print("=" * 70)
print("TRAIN/VALIDATION SPLIT")
print("=" * 70)
print(f"Training set:   {X_train.shape[0]:,} samples ({X_train.shape[0]/len(y)*100:.1f}%)")
print(f"Validation set: {X_val.shape[0]:,} samples ({X_val.shape[0]/len(y)*100:.1f}%)")
print(f"\nFeatures: {X_train.shape[1]}")

# Check class distribution
train_default_rate = y_train.mean() * 100
val_default_rate = y_val.mean() * 100
print(f"\nTrain default rate:      {train_default_rate:.2f}%")
print(f"Validation default rate: {val_default_rate:.2f}%")
print("=" * 70)
```

## Logistic Regression Model

### Train the Model

```{python}
from sklearn.linear_model import LogisticRegression
from sklearn.metrics import roc_curve, auc
import time

print("Training Logistic Regression model...")
print("(This may take a few minutes with 300K+ samples and 200+ features)")

start_time = time.time()

# Train logistic regression with balanced class weights
lr_model = LogisticRegression(
    max_iter=1000,
    random_state=42,
    class_weight='balanced',  # Handle class imbalance
    solver='lbfgs',
    n_jobs=-1  # Use all CPU cores
)

lr_model.fit(X_train, y_train)

training_time = time.time() - start_time

print(f"\n✅ Model trained in {training_time:.2f} seconds")
```

### Evaluate on Validation Set

```{python}
# Make predictions
y_pred_val = lr_model.predict(X_val)
y_prob_val = lr_model.predict_proba(X_val)[:, 1]  # Probability of class 1 (default)

# Calculate metrics
lr_accuracy = accuracy_score(y_val, y_pred_val)
lr_auc = roc_auc_score(y_val, y_prob_val)

# Calculate ROC curve
fpr_lr, tpr_lr, thresholds_lr = roc_curve(y_val, y_prob_val)

print("=" * 70)
print("LOGISTIC REGRESSION - VALIDATION RESULTS")
print("=" * 70)
print(f"\nAccuracy: {lr_accuracy:.4f} ({lr_accuracy*100:.2f}%)")
print(f"AUC-ROC:  {lr_auc:.4f}")
print(f"\nImprovement over baseline:")
print(f"  • Accuracy: {(lr_accuracy - baseline_accuracy)*100:+.2f} percentage points")
print(f"  • AUC:      {(lr_auc - baseline_auc):+.4f}")

print("\nConfusion Matrix:")
print(confusion_matrix(y_val, y_pred_val))

print("\nClassification Report:")
print(classification_report(y_val, y_pred_val, target_names=["Repaid", "Default"]))
print("=" * 70)
```

### Visualize ROC Curve

```{python}
# Compare ROC curves: Baseline vs Logistic Regression
roc_comparison = pd.DataFrame({
    'FPR': np.concatenate([[0, 1], fpr_lr]),
    'TPR': np.concatenate([[0, 1], tpr_lr]),
    'Model': ['Baseline']*2 + ['Logistic Regression']*len(fpr_lr)
})

(
    ggplot(roc_comparison, aes(x='FPR', y='TPR', color='Model'))
    + geom_line(size=1.5)
    + geom_abline(intercept=0, slope=1, linetype='dashed', color='gray', alpha=0.3)
    + labs(
        title='ROC Curve: Logistic Regression vs Baseline',
        x='False Positive Rate',
        y='True Positive Rate (Recall)',
        subtitle=f'Logistic Regression AUC={lr_auc:.4f} | Baseline AUC={baseline_auc:.4f}'
    )
    + scale_color_manual(values=['#e74c3c', '#2ecc71'])
    + theme_minimal()
    + theme(figure_size=(10, 6))
)
```

## Random Forest Model

Random Forest is an ensemble method that often performs well on imbalanced datasets and can capture non-linear relationships.

### Train Random Forest

```{python}
from sklearn.ensemble import RandomForestClassifier

print("Training Random Forest model...")
print("(This may take several minutes with large dataset)")

start_time = time.time()

# Train Random Forest with balanced class weights
rf_model = RandomForestClassifier(
    n_estimators=100,        # Number of trees
    max_depth=20,            # Limit depth to prevent overfitting
    min_samples_split=100,   # Require more samples to split
    min_samples_leaf=50,     # Require more samples in leaf nodes
    class_weight='balanced', # Handle class imbalance
    random_state=42,
    n_jobs=-1,               # Use all CPU cores
    verbose=1                # Show progress
)

rf_model.fit(X_train, y_train)

training_time_rf = time.time() - start_time

print(f"\n✅ Random Forest trained in {training_time_rf:.2f} seconds")
```

### Evaluate Random Forest

```{python}
# Make predictions
y_pred_val_rf = rf_model.predict(X_val)
y_prob_val_rf = rf_model.predict_proba(X_val)[:, 1]

# Calculate metrics
rf_accuracy = accuracy_score(y_val, y_pred_val_rf)
rf_auc = roc_auc_score(y_val, y_prob_val_rf)

# Calculate ROC curve
fpr_rf, tpr_rf, thresholds_rf = roc_curve(y_val, y_prob_val_rf)

print("=" * 70)
print("RANDOM FOREST - VALIDATION RESULTS")
print("=" * 70)
print(f"\nAccuracy: {rf_accuracy:.4f} ({rf_accuracy*100:.2f}%)")
print(f"AUC-ROC:  {rf_auc:.4f}")
print(f"\nComparison to Logistic Regression:")
print(f"  • Accuracy: {(rf_accuracy - lr_accuracy)*100:+.2f} percentage points")
print(f"  • AUC:      {(rf_auc - lr_auc):+.4f}")

print("\nConfusion Matrix:")
print(confusion_matrix(y_val, y_pred_val_rf))

print("\nClassification Report:")
print(classification_report(y_val, y_pred_val_rf, target_names=["Repaid", "Default"]))
print("=" * 70)
```

### Compare All Models

```{python}
# Create comparison table
model_comparison = pd.DataFrame({
    'Model': ['Baseline (Majority)', 'Logistic Regression', 'Random Forest'],
    'Accuracy': [baseline_accuracy, lr_accuracy, rf_accuracy],
    'AUC': [baseline_auc, lr_auc, rf_auc],
    'Training Time (s)': [0, training_time, training_time_rf]
})

print("\n" + "=" * 70)
print("MODEL COMPARISON SUMMARY")
print("=" * 70)
model_comparison
```

```{python}
              ['Logistic Regression']*len(fpr_lr) +

(
    ggplot(roc_all, aes(x='FPR', y='TPR', color='Model'))
```

## Handling Class Imbalance: Advanced Strategies

So far we've used `class_weight='balanced'` which adjusts the loss function to penalize minority class errors more heavily. Let's explore other techniques:

### Strategy Comparison

1. **Class Weighting** (already tried) - Adjust model loss function
2. **SMOTE** - Synthetic Minority Over-sampling Technique
3. **Random Under-sampling** - Reduce majority class
4. **Combination** - SMOTE + Under-sampling

### Install imbalanced-learn

```{python}
import sys
import subprocess

# Install imbalanced-learn for SMOTE
subprocess.check_call([sys.executable, "-m", "pip", "install", "imbalanced-learn", "--quiet"])
print("✅ imbalanced-learn installed!")
```

### Apply SMOTE to Training Data

```{python}
from imblearn.over_sampling import SMOTE
from imblearn.under_sampling import RandomUnderSampler
from imblearn.pipeline import Pipeline as ImbPipeline

print("Original training set distribution:")
print(f"  Class 0 (Repaid):  {(y_train == 0).sum():,} ({(y_train == 0).mean()*100:.2f}%)")
print(f"  Class 1 (Default): {(y_train == 1).sum():,} ({(y_train == 1).mean()*100:.2f}%)")

# Apply SMOTE
print("\nApplying SMOTE to balance classes...")
smote = SMOTE(random_state=42, n_jobs=-1)
X_train_smote, y_train_smote = smote.fit_resample(X_train, y_train)

print("\nAfter SMOTE:")
print(f"  Class 0 (Repaid):  {(y_train_smote == 0).sum():,} ({(y_train_smote == 0).mean()*100:.2f}%)")
print(f"  Class 1 (Default): {(y_train_smote == 1).sum():,} ({(y_train_smote == 1).mean()*100:.2f}%)")
print(f"\nTotal samples increased from {len(y_train):,} to {len(y_train_smote):,}")
```

### Train Random Forest with SMOTE

```{python}
print("Training Random Forest with SMOTE-balanced data...")

start_time = time.time()

# Train without class_weight since data is now balanced
rf_smote = RandomForestClassifier(
    n_estimators=100,
    max_depth=20,
    min_samples_split=100,
    min_samples_leaf=50,
    random_state=42,
    n_jobs=-1,
    verbose=1
)

rf_smote.fit(X_train_smote, y_train_smote)

training_time_smote = time.time() - start_time

print(f"\n✅ Model trained in {training_time_smote:.2f} seconds")
```

### Evaluate SMOTE Model

```{python}
# Make predictions
y_pred_val_smote = rf_smote.predict(X_val)
y_prob_val_smote = rf_smote.predict_proba(X_val)[:, 1]

# Calculate metrics
smote_accuracy = accuracy_score(y_val, y_pred_val_smote)
smote_auc = roc_auc_score(y_val, y_prob_val_smote)

# Calculate ROC curve
fpr_smote, tpr_smote, _ = roc_curve(y_val, y_prob_val_smote)

print("=" * 70)
print("RANDOM FOREST + SMOTE - VALIDATION RESULTS")
print("=" * 70)
print(f"\nAccuracy: {smote_accuracy:.4f} ({smote_accuracy*100:.2f}%)")
print(f"AUC-ROC:  {smote_auc:.4f}")
print(f"\nComparison to RF with class_weight='balanced':")
print(f"  • Accuracy: {(smote_accuracy - rf_accuracy)*100:+.2f} percentage points")
print(f"  • AUC:      {(smote_auc - rf_auc):+.4f}")

print("\nConfusion Matrix:")
print(confusion_matrix(y_val, y_pred_val_smote))

print("\nClassification Report:")
print(classification_report(y_val, y_pred_val_smote, target_names=["Repaid", "Default"]))
print("=" * 70)
```

### Try Under-sampling

```{python}
print("Applying Random Under-sampling...")

# Under-sample majority class to match minority class
undersampler = RandomUnderSampler(random_state=42)
X_train_under, y_train_under = undersampler.fit_resample(X_train, y_train)

print(f"\nOriginal: {len(y_train):,} samples")
print(f"After under-sampling: {len(y_train_under):,} samples")
print(f"  Class 0 (Repaid):  {(y_train_under == 0).sum():,} ({(y_train_under == 0).mean()*100:.2f}%)")
print(f"  Class 1 (Default): {(y_train_under == 1).sum():,} ({(y_train_under == 1).mean()*100:.2f}%)")
```

```{python}
print("Training Random Forest with under-sampled data...")

start_time = time.time()

rf_under = RandomForestClassifier(
    n_estimators=100,
    max_depth=20,
    min_samples_split=50,  # Adjusted for smaller dataset
    min_samples_leaf=25,
    random_state=42,
    n_jobs=-1,
    verbose=1
)

rf_under.fit(X_train_under, y_train_under)

training_time_under = time.time() - start_time

print(f"\n✅ Model trained in {training_time_under:.2f} seconds")
```

### Evaluate Under-sampling Model

```{python}

y_pred_val_under = rf_under.predict(X_val)
y_prob_val_under = rf_under.predict_proba(X_val)[:, 1]

# Calculate metrics
under_accuracy = accuracy_score(y_val, y_pred_val_under)
under_auc = roc_auc_score(y_val, y_prob_val_under)

# Calculate ROC curve
fpr_under, tpr_under, _ = roc_curve(y_val, y_prob_val_under)

print("=" * 70)
print("RANDOM FOREST + UNDER-SAMPLING - VALIDATION RESULTS")
print("=" * 70)
print(f"\nAccuracy: {under_accuracy:.4f} ({under_accuracy*100:.2f}%)")
print(f"AUC-ROC:  {under_auc:.4f}")

print("\nConfusion Matrix:")
print(confusion_matrix(y_val, y_pred_val_under))

print("\nClassification Report:")
print(classification_report(y_val, y_pred_val_under, target_names=["Repaid", "Default"]))
print("=" * 70)
```

## Hyperparameter Tuning

Let's optimize the Random Forest (our best model) using Randomized Search CV on a subsample for efficiency.

### Create Subsample for Tuning

```{python}
from sklearn.model_selection import RandomizedSearchCV
from scipy.stats import randint, uniform

# Create a 5K subsample for faster tuning
np.random.seed(42)
subsample_idx = np.random.choice(len(X_train), size=5000, replace=False)
X_train_sub = X_train.iloc[subsample_idx]
y_train_sub = y_train[subsample_idx]

print(f"Subsample for tuning: {len(X_train_sub):,} samples")
print(f"Class distribution in subsample:")
print(f"  Class 0 (Repaid):  {(y_train_sub == 0).sum():,} ({(y_train_sub == 0).mean()*100:.2f}%)")
print(f"  Class 1 (Default): {(y_train_sub == 1).sum():,} ({(y_train_sub == 1).mean()*100:.2f}%)")
```

### Define Hyperparameter Grid

```{python}
# Define parameter distributions for randomized search
param_distributions = {
    'n_estimators': [100, 150, 200, 250],
    'max_depth': [15, 20, 25, 30, None],
    'min_samples_split': randint(50, 200),
    'min_samples_leaf': randint(20, 100),
    'max_features': ['sqrt', 'log2', 0.3, 0.5],
    'bootstrap': [True, False]
}

print("Hyperparameter search space:")
for param, values in param_distributions.items():
    print(f"  • {param}: {values}")
```

### Run Randomized Search

```{python}
print("\nRunning Randomized Search CV...")
print("  • Subsample size: 5,000")
print("  • CV folds: 3")
print("  • Number of iterations: 20")
print("  • Scoring: ROC AUC")
print("\n(This will take several minutes...)")

start_time = time.time()

# Create base model
rf_base = RandomForestClassifier(
    class_weight='balanced',
    random_state=42,
    n_jobs=-1
)

# Randomized search with 3-fold CV
random_search = RandomizedSearchCV(
    estimator=rf_base,
    param_distributions=param_distributions,
    n_iter=20,  # Number of parameter settings sampled
    cv=3,  # 3-fold cross-validation
    scoring='roc_auc',
    random_state=42,
    n_jobs=-1,
    verbose=2,
    return_train_score=True
)

random_search.fit(X_train_sub, y_train_sub)

tuning_time = time.time() - start_time

print(f"\n✅ Hyperparameter tuning complete in {tuning_time:.2f} seconds")
```

### Best Parameters Found

```{python}
print("=" * 70)
print("HYPERPARAMETER TUNING RESULTS")
print("=" * 70)

print("\n🏆 Best Parameters:")
for param, value in random_search.best_params_.items():
    print(f"  • {param}: {value}")

print(f"\n📊 Best CV Score (AUC): {random_search.best_score_:.4f}")
print(f"   Mean CV time per fold: {random_search.cv_results_['mean_fit_time'][random_search.best_index_]:.2f}s")
```

### Analyze Parameter Importance

```{python}
# Get CV results
cv_results = pd.DataFrame(random_search.cv_results_)

# Show top 5 parameter combinations
top_5 = cv_results.nsmallest(5, 'rank_test_score')[
    ['params', 'mean_test_score', 'std_test_score', 'mean_fit_time']
]

print("\nTop 5 Parameter Combinations:")
print(top_5.to_string(index=False))
```

### Train Final Model with Best Parameters

```{python}
print("\n" + "=" * 70)
print("TRAINING FINAL MODEL WITH BEST PARAMETERS")
print("=" * 70)
print(f"Training on full training set: {len(X_train):,} samples")

start_time = time.time()

# Create final model with best parameters
rf_final = RandomForestClassifier(
    **random_search.best_params_,
    class_weight='balanced',
    random_state=42,
    n_jobs=-1,
    verbose=1
)

rf_final.fit(X_train, y_train)

training_time_final = time.time() - start_time

print(f"\n✅ Final model trained in {training_time_final:.2f} seconds")
```

### Evaluate Final Tuned Model

```{python}
# Make predictions
y_pred_val_final = rf_final.predict(X_val)
y_prob_val_final = rf_final.predict_proba(X_val)[:, 1]

# Calculate metrics
final_accuracy = accuracy_score(y_val, y_pred_val_final)
final_auc = roc_auc_score(y_val, y_prob_val_final)

# Calculate ROC curve
fpr_final, tpr_final, _ = roc_curve(y_val, y_prob_val_final)

print("=" * 70)
print("FINAL TUNED MODEL - VALIDATION RESULTS")
print("=" * 70)
print(f"\nAccuracy: {final_accuracy:.4f} ({final_accuracy*100:.2f}%)")
print(f"AUC-ROC:  {final_auc:.4f}")
print(f"\nImprovement over default Random Forest:")
print(f"  • Accuracy: {(final_accuracy - rf_accuracy)*100:+.2f} percentage points")
print(f"  • AUC:      {(final_auc - rf_auc):+.4f}")

print("\nConfusion Matrix:")
print(confusion_matrix(y_val, y_pred_val_final))

print("\nClassification Report:")
print(classification_report(y_val, y_pred_val_final, target_names=["Repaid", "Default"]))
print("=" * 70)
```

## Adding Credit Card Balance Features

Based on EDA findings, we identified that credit card payment behavior is highly predictive of default risk. Let's enhance our model by adding features from `credit_card_balance.csv`.

### What Credit Card Features Add

Credit card data provides monthly snapshots showing:
- **Credit utilization** (how much of limit is used)
- **Payment discipline** (days past due patterns)
- **Balance trends** (increasing/decreasing debt)
- **Drawing behavior** (ATM withdrawals, cash advances)

These are strong default predictors!

### Update R Pipeline

We added `aggregate_credit_card()` function to `Data_Preparation_and_Feature_Engineering.R` which creates 23 new features:
- CC_AVG_UTILIZATION, CC_MAX_UTILIZATION, CC_HIGH_UTIL_PCT
- CC_DPD_COUNT, CC_DPD_PCT, CC_LATE_COUNT, CC_MAX_DPD
- CC_AVG_BALANCE, CC_BALANCE_TREND
- CC_AVG_PAYMENT, CC_PAYMENT_RATIO
- CC_ATM_RATE, CC_DRAWING_RATE
- And more...

Then regenerated fully imputed data:

```r
# In run_full_pipeline.R, we enabled:
train_result <- prepare_data_pipeline(
  app_data = train,
  include_credit_card = TRUE,  # NEW!
  final_imputation = TRUE
)
```

### Load Enhanced Data

```{python}

print(f"\n{len(cc_features)} Credit Card Features:")
for i, feat in enumerate(cc_features[:10], 1):
    print(f"  {i}. {feat}")
if len(cc_features) > 10:
    print(f"  ... and {len(cc_features) - 10} more")
```

### Prepare Enhanced Data

```{python}
# Same preparation as before
feature_cols_enh = [col for col in df_train_enhanced.columns if col not in ["SK_ID_CURR", "TARGET"]]

X_enh = df_train_enhanced.select(feature_cols_enh)
y_enh = df_train_enhanced.get_column("TARGET").to_numpy()

# Identify and encode categorical columns
cat_cols_enh = [col for col in X_enh.columns if X_enh[col].dtype == pl.Utf8]
X_enh_pd = X_enh.to_pandas()
X_enh_encoded = pd.get_dummies(X_enh_pd, columns=cat_cols_enh, drop_first=True)

print(f"Enhanced features after encoding: {X_enh_encoded.shape[1]}")

# Train/Val split (same random_state=42 for fair comparison)
X_train_enh, X_val_enh, y_train_enh, y_val_enh = train_test_split(
    X_enh_encoded,
    y_enh,
    test_size=0.2,
    random_state=42,
    stratify=y_enh
)

print(f"Train: {X_train_enh.shape[0]:,} samples, {X_train_enh.shape[1]} features")
print(f"Val: {X_val_enh.shape[0]:,} samples")
```

### Train Enhanced Model

```{python}
print("Training Random Forest with tuned hyperparameters on ENHANCED data...")

rf_enhanced = RandomForestClassifier(
```

### Key Insights

**Impact of Credit Card Features:**

1. **AUC improved** from 0.7624 → 0.7650 (+0.0026)
2. **Caught 38 more defaults** (2,632 vs 2,594 out of 4,965)
3. **Most important CC features:**
   - CC_HIGH_UTIL_PCT - Frequency of high utilization (>80%)
   - CC_DRAWING_RATE - How aggressively they draw on credit
   - CC_AVG_UTILIZATION - Average credit utilization rate
   - CC_PAYMENT_RATIO - Payment vs balance ratio

4. **Why it works:** Credit card behavior reveals:
   - Financial stress (high utilization)
   - Payment discipline (DPD patterns)
   - Debt accumulation (balance trends)
   - Cash needs (ATM withdrawals)

**This enhanced model is now our best performer and ready for test predictions!**

## Generate Test Set Predictions

Now let's use our best model (Enhanced Random Forest with AUC=0.7650) to make predictions on the test set for Kaggle submission.

### Load Test Data

```{python}
# Load the enhanced test data (with credit card features)
df_test = pl.read_csv(
    "application_test_fully_imputed.csv",
    infer_schema_length=None
)

print("=" * 70)
print("TEST DATA")
print("=" * 70)
print(f"Shape: {df_test.shape}")
print(f"Missing values: {df_test.null_count().sum_horizontal()[0]}")
print(f"Columns match training: {df_test.shape[1] == df_train_enhanced.shape[1] - 1}")  # -1 for TARGET
```

### Prepare Test Data

```{python}
# Save SK_ID_CURR for submission
test_ids = df_test.get_column("SK_ID_CURR").to_numpy()

# Prepare features (same process as training)
feature_cols_test = [col for col in df_test.columns if col != "SK_ID_CURR"]

X_test = df_test.select(feature_cols_test)

# Identify and encode categorical columns
cat_cols_test = [col for col in X_test.columns if X_test[col].dtype == pl.Utf8]
X_test_pd = X_test.to_pandas()
X_test_encoded = pd.get_dummies(X_test_pd, columns=cat_cols_test, drop_first=True)

print(f"\nTest data prepared:")
print(f"  Samples: {X_test_encoded.shape[0]:,}")
print(f"  Features after encoding: {X_test_encoded.shape[1]}")

# Ensure test has same columns as training
# Add missing columns with 0s (dummy variables that didn't appear in test)
missing_cols = set(X_enh_encoded.columns) - set(X_test_encoded.columns)
for col in missing_cols:
    X_test_encoded[col] = 0

# Remove extra columns (dummy variables that didn't appear in training)
extra_cols = set(X_test_encoded.columns) - set(X_enh_encoded.columns)
X_test_encoded = X_test_encoded.drop(columns=list(extra_cols))

# Reorder columns to match training
X_test_encoded = X_test_encoded[X_enh_encoded.columns]

print(f"  Final features (aligned with training): {X_test_encoded.shape[1]}")
print(f"  Column alignment check: {list(X_test_encoded.columns) == list(X_enh_encoded.columns)}")
```

### Make Predictions

```{python}
print("\nGenerating predictions on test set...")

# Predict probabilities of default (class 1)
test_predictions = rf_enhanced.predict_proba(X_test_encoded)[:, 1]

print(f"✅ Predictions generated for {len(test_predictions):,} test samples")
print(f"\nPrediction statistics:")
print(f"  Min probability: {test_predictions.min():.4f}")
print(f"  Max probability: {test_predictions.max():.4f}")
print(f"  Mean probability: {test_predictions.mean():.4f}")
print(f"  Median probability: {np.median(test_predictions):.4f}")

# Show distribution of predicted probabilities
print(f"\nPrediction distribution:")
print(f"  < 0.1 (very low risk):  {(test_predictions < 0.1).sum():,} ({(test_predictions < 0.1).mean()*100:.1f}%)")
print(f"  0.1 - 0.2 (low risk):    {((test_predictions >= 0.1) & (test_predictions < 0.2)).sum():,} ({((test_predictions >= 0.1) & (test_predictions < 0.2)).mean()*100:.1f}%)")
print(f"  0.2 - 0.5 (medium risk): {((test_predictions >= 0.2) & (test_predictions < 0.5)).sum():,} ({((test_predictions >= 0.2) & (test_predictions < 0.5)).mean()*100:.1f}%)")
print(f"  >= 0.5 (high risk):      {(test_predictions >= 0.5).sum():,} ({(test_predictions >= 0.5).mean()*100:.1f}%)")
```

### Visualize Prediction Distribution
